title: Build and Compose Shapes: Put Shapes Together
seo_title: Kindergarten Composing Shapes Worksheets: Build Shapes and Make Bigger Shapes
standard_text: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, “Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?”
meta_desc: Free kindergarten worksheets on composing shapes: build shapes with sticks and clay balls, find the small shapes inside a big shape, count the pieces, and put triangles and squares together to make squares, rectangles and hexagons. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Small shapes can fit together to make a bigger shape.
key_sub: 2 triangles make a square, 2 squares make a rectangle, 6 triangles make a hexagon.
body_html:
Build shapes with sticks and clay

Each stick is a side. Each clay ball is a corner.

ShapeSticksClay balls
Triangle33
Square44
Rectangle44
Hexagon66

Put small shapes together

Small shapes can fit together, with no gaps, to make a bigger shape.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Naming the pieces instead of the big shapeLook at the outside line for the big shape
Counting a piece twiceTouch each piece once
Leaving gaps between piecesSlide the sides together so they touch

faq.a: It means putting small shapes together to make a bigger shape. For example, 2 triangles can make a square and 2 squares can make a rectangle.

faq.q: Why do kindergartners build shapes with sticks and clay?
faq.a: Building a shape shows its parts. Each stick is a side and each clay ball is a corner, so children learn why a triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

faq.q: How can I practice at home?
faq.a: Use toothpicks and play dough, or cut paper squares into triangles and put them back together. Pattern blocks and tangrams are great too.

faq.q: How does this help later in math?
faq.a: Seeing shapes made of smaller shapes helps with fractions (halves and fourths) and area in later grades.

items.q: How many sticks make this triangle?
items.e: Each side is 1 stick. A triangle has 3 sides, so it needs 3 sticks.

items.q: What shape did the sticks make?
items.e: It has 3 sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle.

items.q: How many sticks make this square?
items.e: Each side is 1 stick. A square has 4 sides, so it needs 4 sticks.

items.q: What shape did the sticks make?
items.e: It has 4 sides and 4 corners that are all the same length. It is a square.

items.q: How many clay balls hold this triangle together?

items.q: How many clay balls hold this square together?

items.q: Can you make a circle with straight sticks?
